reading.body:
Meta's Prineville campus in Crook County, Oregon is the state's largest hyperscale data center facility by investment and employment footprint, though it does not publish its power capacity. Meta has committed $2B+ to the site since groundbreaking in 2010 and operates it with 350+ permanent staff, indicating sustained expansion beyond initial construction. The company has tied its electricity supply entirely to renewable energy and is coordinating a 977-megawatt renewable energy project in the state to match campus loads.

Oregon has published power figures for only eight of its 133 mapped data center facilities, totaling 156.6 megawatts. Prineville ranks ninth among all mapped Oregon facilities by the operator specs this site has read, suggesting either that the Prineville campus operates below the published MW threshold or that Meta, unlike some other operators, does not disclose its power consumption. Without published IT load, the campus's contribution to state AI scaling capacity cannot be calculated directly from available data.

The facility's water and energy commitments signal operational maturity and scale, but the absence of published power figures limits its visibility as a constraint on AI compute availability. The 977-megawatt renewable energy project Meta supports indicates the company views Prineville as a site of significant ongoing demand. Rank within the state's mapped landscape depends on capacity figures Meta has chosen not to publish.
